system_overview: This specification models a basic grow-only counter Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT). Each node in a distributed system maintains a vector of counters, one per node. Nodes can increment their own counter and propagate state to other nodes through gossip. The specification is part of a collection illustrating how ordinarily-infinite monotonic systems can be made finite for model checking.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a set of distributed nodes, each maintaining a local view of every node's counter value. Nodes act both as writers (incrementing their own counter) and as gossip participants (sending and receiving state updates to synchronize their views).
state_variables: The system tracks a two-dimensional mapping from each node to its view of every node's counter value. Each node maintains a vector indexed by all nodes, where each entry is a natural number representing that node's current counter value as known to the viewing node.
initial_state: All counter values in all nodes' views are initialized to zero. Every node's view of every other node's counter starts at zero.
actions: There are two types of transitions: (1) Increment: a node increments its own entry in its local counter vector by one. Only a node's own counter entry in its own view is modified. (2) Gossip: one node sends its entire counter vector to another node. The receiving node updates each entry in its view to the maximum of its current value and the sender's value for that entry. This merge operation ensures values only increase.
safety_properties: Each node's own view of its own counter must always be at least as large as any other node's view of that counter. In other words, a node always has the most up-to-date value of its own counter. Additionally, all counter values must remain non-negative natural numbers conforming to the expected type structure.
liveness_properties: Convergence: the system must repeatedly reach states where all nodes have identical counter vectors. That is, infinitely often, all nodes agree on every counter value. Monotonicity: counter values as observed by any node must never decrease across transitions.
model_bounds: The set of nodes is declared as a constant. For model checking, this is typically instantiated as a small finite set (for example, three nodes). The finite monotonic technique bounds counter values by limiting the maximum divergence between the lowest and highest counter values across the system.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on all gossip actions between every pair of nodes, ensuring that gossip will eventually occur whenever it is enabled. Additionally, the specification assumes that from some point onwards, only gossip actions are performed (increments happen only finitely often). This combination ensures eventual convergence. The overall specification with these fairness conditions is machine closed despite the second condition not being a standard fairness assumption.
